newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates close steady on low demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates close steady on low demand.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates closed steady on Tuesday on low demand for spinners for the 1996/97 (July-June) crop are likely to open unchanged on Wednesday, dealers at the Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) said.
The spinners are buying the new 1997/98 crop while exporters are buying the old crop for shipments, one dealer said.
The rates are likely to remain range-bound despite rains in the Punjab province, he said.
In the kerb market, the NIAB-78 variety was quoted for 2,375/2,380 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), the K-68 for 2,575/2,585 and the MNH-93 at 2,580/2,590.

The KCA said exporters had shipped 125,515 bales (375 lbs each) of cotton by June 28 compared to 1.82 million bales in the same time a year ago. Exporters had registered contracts for the export of 164,756 bales by July 8 compared to 2.32 million bales in the same time a year ago.
